name: Slime Mold
description: Physarum polycephalum: network intelligence without neurons. Optimizes nutrient transport networks that rediscover human-engineered infrastructure layouts. Pulsatile cytoplasmic flow encodes memory through tube diameter reinforcement.

core_attributes.pattern: acellular network optimization, pulsatile memory encoding, infrastructure emergence

scope.definition: Network optimization efficiency of Physarum polycephalum tube network connecting food sources — ratio of achieved network total tube length to Steiner minimum spanning tree (theoretical optimum) connecting same nodes.

evidence.source: Tero et al. (2010) 'Rules for biologically inspired adaptive network design', Science 327:439-442.
cross_domain_examples: Physarum recreates Tokyo rail network topology (0.94 efficiency ratio) on food-source map of cities
achieves near-Steiner-minimum networks within 26 hours without global information or central control
ant pheromone networks: analogous distributed shortest-path optimization without global planning
Steiner problem is NP-hard for computers — Physarum achieves near-optimal in polynomial time

scope.falsifiability: If Physarum tube networks are consistently >30% longer than Steiner minimum trees across 20+ food-source configurations, the near-optimal network claim is not supported.
scope.measurement_limits: Network quality degrades on non-planar substrates and under simultaneous multiple food-source additions. The Tokyo experiment used a highly constrained 2D planar layout — complex 3D networks may show lower optimality.
